newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to keep control of oil, product pipelines.
newsitem.headline: Russia to keep control of oil, product pipelines.

text.p: Russia will retain a majority stake in Transneft, the monopoly for oil and oil product pipelines, First Deputy Fuel and Energy Minister Sergei Kiriyenko said on Tuesday.
"At the moment, work is taking place on the privatisation (of Transneft)," he told a news briefing. "It is necessary to privatise it, but the controlling share will be held by the government."

He said Russia would always want to have ultimate control of a company of such strategic importance, adding, "handing over control must never happen, because guaranteeing the energy security of the country is the sole aim of the company."
Fuel and Energy Minister Boris Nemtsov is in charge of revamping Russia's natural monopolies, including Transneft, gas monopoly Gazprom and electricity group UES (Unified Energy System).
Russia has done more to restructure its gas and electricity sectors than its railways and pipeline monopolies.
Trasneft's crude oil pipeline system stretches for 50,000 km (31,000 miles), with product pipelines covering 20,500 km (12,700 miles).
